en.headline: Disgusting Food Museum continues at Kai Tak AIRSIDE until late November
en.dek: The Swedish exhibition displays more than 80 polarising foods from 35 countries with multi-sensory zones and a tasting bar at Gate33 Gallery.
body: The Disgusting Food Museum, a Swedish exhibition that has attracted more than 500,000 visitors internationally, is open at Gate33 Gallery in AIRSIDE, Kai Tak, until 26 November.

According to the venue, the show presents more than 80 foods from 35 countries across five thematic zones, including fermented shark, cheese containing live maggots, insects and cultivated meat, together with scent installations and interactive displays that explore cultural differences in what people consider edible.

Opening hours are noon to 7pm Monday to Thursday and 11am to 8pm on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Tickets start from HK$48, and a tasting bar allows visitors to try selected items under staff guidance.

zh.headline: 嘔心食物博物館啟德AIRSIDE展出至11月下旬
zh.dek: 瑞典展覽在GATE33藝文館展出逾80款來自35國的爭議美食，設多感官體驗及試食吧，至11月26日。
body: 來自瑞典的嘔心食物博物館目前在啟德AIRSIDE三樓GATE33藝文館展出，至11月26日止。展覽曾在多個城市巡迴，吸引逾50萬人次入場，香港為首次舉辦。
場地資料指，展覽搜羅超過80款來自35個國家的奇葩美食，涵蓋活蛆芝士、發酵鯊魚、昆蟲及培植肉等，分為五大主題區域，透過互動展品、氣味裝置及多感官體驗，讓觀眾認識不同飲食文化背後的故事。
開放時間為星期一至四中午12時至晚上7時，星期五至日及公眾假期上午11時至晚上8時。門票由48元起，設有試食吧，觀眾可在工作人員指導下親嘗部分食材。
